newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl says Germany will pull out stops to reach EMU.
newsitem.headline: Kohl says Germany will pull out stops to reach EMU.

text.p: Chancellor Helmut Kohl said on Saturday Germany would do everything it could to meet the criteria for European economic and monetary union (EMU).

Kohl, according to the text of a speech he was to deliver to a farmers' association in the southern town of Bockenheim, said EMU was an important step en route to political union in the EU. He said delay in the single currency launch would endanger the integration process in Europe.

"We have to take advantage of the historical chance we have with the introduction of the euro," Kohl said. "The federal government will do everything it can to fulfil the stability criteria as outlined in the Maastricht Treaty."
Kohl added: "We need EMU as a step on the way to political union."
He said delaying the euro's launch from its scheduled start in 1999 would endanger the integration process and harm German exporters.
"To delay the question of the euro would endanger what we have achieved so far in the European integration process and would also cause great difficulties for the German export economy," Kohl said.
